title: A key with no match on an inactive relationship gives the one side the blank row
query: "On the blank row", CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], ISBLANK ( 'Date'[Date] ) ),
"Delivered on the blank row", CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], ISBLANK ( 'Date'[Date] ), USERELATIONSHIP ( Sales[DeliveryDate], 'Date'[Date] ) )

source.quote: Inactive relationships are also expanded, even when the relationship isn't used by a calculation.
source.supports: an inactive relationship is expanded like an active one

source.quote: When a matching value from the "many" to the "one" side doesn't exist, a blank virtual row is added to the "one" side table.
source.supports: the expansion adds the blank row for a key with no match

source.quote: The blank row is a special row added to a table, in case the table is on the one-side of a strong relationship and the relationship is invalid.
source.supports: VALUES counts the blank row and DISTINCT doesn't

alternative: If an inactive relationship adds no blank row (Learn's note read as about the stored join only), 'Date' has none: Values 6, Distinct 6, and the last two BLANK.
derivation: Sale 7 is delivered on 2024-04-15, which 'Date' lacks; its order date 2024-03-01 is there, so the active relationship has no orphan. By Learn's note the inactive relationship Sales[DeliveryDate] -> 'Date'[Date] is expanded too, so 'Date' gets the blank row: VALUES has the 6 dates and the blank row (7), DISTINCT the 6 dates. Through the active relationship no sale reaches the blank row: BLANK. With USERELATIONSHIP on the delivery date, sale 7 (100) lands on it.
